title: The True Face of the Third Force
next_chapter_hook: As that voice extended the invitation, Chen Ji felt the Tianji Record Fragment in his hand tremble violently—as if responding to some ancient summoning.

text.content: Beyond the Heavenly Realm Barrier, an ancient aura awakened like a beast that had slumbered for ten thousand years. That gaze held no hostility, but rather a scrutiny beyond time, as if some existence was observing this chess game on a scale of millennia. The Tianji Record Fragment in Chen Ji's hand suddenly grew scalding hot, the runes on its surface flowing in trajectories never before seen—a sign that the sealed entity was attempting to resonate with it.

The gazes of three factions converged on Chen Ji, but that ancient aura shattered all their schemes. Han Lie of the Xuanwu Sect knit his brows tightly, feeling a suppression from deep within his bloodline; Ling Yuan of the Tianqing Sect's fingers trembled slightly in his sleeves, as if recalling some past he wished not to face; while Ye Qing's eyes snapped wide open, her Demonic Path perception screaming warnings—an existence beyond any known threat level.

In the instant when everyone held their breath, the space beyond the barrier was torn apart by an invisible hand. A figure stepped forward slowly—it was a man who appeared no more than twenty years old, his features hauntingly beautiful, surrounded by pale golden mist, each step causing fine cracks to spread through the void beneath his feet. His gaze swept over the three factions like still water, yet all felt a dizziness as if facing an abyss.

dialogue.content: "There's no need for alarm, everyone. I've waited for this day far too long." The man's voice was clear and resonant, yet it sounded simultaneously in each person's ear. "My name is Shi Chen, or rather—I am the only one among the seven Chess Players of ten thousand years ago who was never replaced." His gaze finally settled on Chen Ji, a meaningful smile curving his lips. "Successor of the Tianji Record, I've been waiting for you for a very long time."

text.content: Chen Ji felt the temperature of the Tianji Record Fragment rise abruptly, as if about to ignite. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul in the first page of the Tianji Record fluctuated violently—an emotion Chen Ji had never felt before. Not fear, but rage, a bone-deep fury of betrayal. The name "Shi Chen" had clearly touched some forbidden chord.

Shi Chen's gaze swept across the three calculating veterans, shaking his head lightly: "Ling Yuan, you think you've been scheming for the inheritance of the Tianji Record; Han Lie, you think you possess unrivaled combat power; even the Eye of Heavenly Mandate itself believes it owns the chessboard." His smile carried an indescribable mockery. "Pathetic. You're merely pieces arranged by the Seventh Chess Player—and he is the true variable."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji did not evade Shi Chen's gaze; instead, he took the initiative to speak: "Since you say you've been waiting for me a long time, why not speak plainly—what is the truth from ten thousand years ago? Who is this Seventh Chess Player you speak of?" His voice was calm, but the knuckles of his fingers gripping the Tianji Record had turned white. A truth惊天动地 enough to evoke such wariness from Mo Xiansheng must be earth-shatteringly significant.

text.content: Shi Chen laughed lightly, that laughter carrying ten thousand years of vicissitudes: "Ten thousand years ago, Heavenly Mandate was not as despotic as it is now. It was merely a rule, and rules required Chess Players to maintain them. At that time, seven Chess Players jointly sustained the运转 of Heavenly Secrets. The Tianji Record in your hand is a relic of the First Chess Player." His eyes deepened. "However, the Eye of Heavenly Mandate awakened its own consciousness. It wanted to become the true 'Heaven,' not merely a rule. It began hunting Chess Players."

Ling Yuan's face turned ashen at this moment. He lifted his head abruptly, eyes full of disbelief: "Impossible! How could the Eye of Heavenly Mandate have self-awareness? It's only—" His words stopped abruptly because Shi Chen had already raised his hand, pointing at Ling Yuan's brow center. A golden light entered his Mental Sea, bringing visions from ten thousand years ago: seven Chess Players seated discussing the Dao, while in the void, a massive eye slowly opened—one without the slightest emotion, only an craving for 'absolute authority.'

The image faded, Ling Yuan stumbled backward, muttering to himself: "So that's how it was... so that's how it was..." Han Lie stared at Shi Chen with gritted teeth, his fists clenched so tight they creaked: "Since you know all this, why didn't you stop it? Watching the Heavenly Mandate hunt Chess Players?" Shi Chen glanced at him, that gaze like looking at an ignorant ant: "Because each of those six Chess Players wanted to replace the Eye of Heavenly Mandate. I simply chose the correct side."

At this moment, Chen Ji finally understood something. He looked at the Tianji Record in his hand, then at Shi Chen: "So the Eye of Heavenly Mandate is the ultimate enemy. And you waited for me because—I am the successor of the Tianji Record, and the only one who might oppose it?" Shi Chen nodded: "Throughout the ages, every successor of the Tianji Record has been erased by the Eye of Heavenly Mandate. But you are different. You carry the backup measure left by the Seventh Chess Player."

choice.prompt: Shi Chen's words revealed a shocking truth, but Chen Ji knew well: the more extraordinary the story, the more caution it requires. He must decide his attitude going forward.

choices.description: Since the other party holds the key truth, might as well continue asking questions to verify the authenticity of their words.
choices.visible_reward: Gain More Truth from Ten Thousand Years Ago
choices.risk_hint: Shi Chen Might Be Testing Your True Nature

text.content: Chen Ji slightly nodded, his gaze carrying prudence: "You say I am the only one who might oppose the Eye of Heavenly Mandate, so what exactly is the backup measure left by the Seventh Chess Player? If you truly have sincerity, speak plainly." His questions were precise and sharp, pointing directly to the core.

dialogue.content: A flicker of approval crossed Shi Chen's eyes: "Good question. The Seventh Chess Player—that is, the creator of the Tianji Record—sealed his own resolve into the Tianji Record before his death. That was not a simple inheritance of power, but a 'possibility.' As long as you are strong enough, the Tianji Record can foresee any outcome, including—the outcome of defeating the Eye of Heavenly Mandate."

choices.description: The truth from ten thousand years ago is too shocking, and Shi Chen's stance is ambiguous. One must remain vigilant.

text.content: Chen Ji nodded on the surface, but in secret activated the Tianji Record, wanting to foresee this person's intentions. However, the Tianji Record's reaction made his heart chill—all foresight images regarding Shi Chen were blurred, as if some force was blocking his窥探.

dialogue.content: "Interesting." Chen Ji suddenly laughed. "Since you say you've been waiting for me a long time, you should know my habit—I don't like cooperation seen through a fog. What exactly do you want?" His tone remained peaceful, but the coldness in his eyes made Ling Yuan secretly gasp: When did this young man develop such momentum?

choices.description: No matter how nicely the other party speaks, directly question their true purpose.
choices.visible_reward: Force the Other Party to Reveal Their Cards

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly stepped forward, locking eyes with Shi Chen: "However many years of truth you speak of, I'll暂且不论. But I'm curious—if you say you're the only surviving Chess Player, why didn't you act during the past ten thousand years? Why appear now?" His voice was not loud, yet carried unstoppable sharpness.

dialogue.content: Shi Chen was silent for a moment, then smiled: "Because I've been waiting for the moment when the balance between the Eye of Heavenly Mandate and the Chess Players is broken. Now, three major sects are fighting, the Demonic Path is invading, the Ancient Forbidden Land has opened—all the pieces are in position—and you are the key to starting the final game." His gaze turned sharp. "This is my purpose: help you defeat the Eye of Heavenly Mandate, then—I will remake the rules."

text.content: Remake the rules? Chen Ji coldly smiled in his heart. This is merely another existence wanting to become 'Heaven.' But he didn't say it aloud, continuing to ask: "You say the Tianji Record can foresee the outcome of defeating the Eye of Heavenly Mandate, then what is the cost?" Shi Chen looked at him, his smile deepening: "Cost? Haven't you already known? Every foresight consumes Heavenly Fate. But what you don't know is—to see the complete path to defeating the Eye of Heavenly Mandate requires a Heavenly Fate value足以让任何人瞬间陨落."

Chen Ji's pupils suddenly contracted. The true purpose of Heavenly Fate was actually this. He had always thought the Tianji Record was merely a tool for seeing the future, never expecting its true定位 to be a "God-Slaying Diagram." Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded within the Tianji Record, carrying a trace of bitterness: "I should have told you earlier. The purpose for which the Seventh Chess Player created the Tianji Record was never to peek into Heavenly Secrets—but to break Heavenly Mandate. He sealed his resolve within it, waiting for a successor strong enough to complete his unfinished quest."

choice.prompt: The true purpose of the Tianji Record is revealed, and Chen Ji must decide how to face this heavy truth.

choices.description: Since the Tianji Record was born for this, then accept this path of God-Slaying with composure.
choices.visible_cost: May Pay the Price of Life
choices.risk_hint: The Eye of Heavenly Mandate Won't Sit Idle

text.content: Chen Ji was silent for a long time, finally lifting his head. His eyes held no fear, only a tranquility of having seen through everything: "Since the Tianji Record is indeed a God-Slaying Diagram, then I will be the successor who walks this path." His voice was not loud, yet carried unwavering resolve. "But I will not become anyone's piece—including you."

dialogue.content: Shi Chen burst out laughing, that laughter carrying genuine appreciation: "Good! Worthy of being the one chosen by the Seventh Chess Player. I don't need you to be my piece; I only need you to do one thing—be strong enough, strong enough to face the Eye of Heavenly Mandate directly. As for what comes after—" He paused. "That is a matter for later."

choices.description: No matter how shocking the truth, one cannot easily believe a stranger's words.
choices.risk_hint: Shi Chen May No Longer Disclose More Information

text.content: Chen Ji did not immediately commit, instead continuing to ask: "You've said so much, but how can I be sure this isn't another trap? The Chess Players of ten thousand years ago wanted to replace Heavenly Mandate, and now you want to remake rules. Fundamentally speaking, what essential difference do you have from the Eye of Heavenly Mandate?"

dialogue.content: Shi Chen's smile faltered slightly, then deepened: "Difference? Perhaps there is none. But one thing I can tell you—the Eye of Heavenly Mandate demands absolute obedience, while I only need a strong enough opponent. Victory without an opponent is meaningless." An edge of loneliness actually leaked into his words.

text.content: Just at this moment, the Heavenly Realm Barrier suddenly vibrated violently. An imposing, suffocating aura came from deep within the barrier—that was the will projection of the Eye of Heavenly Mandate. Shi Chen's expression changed slightly: "It has sensed us. It seems our conversation time is running out." He looked at Chen Ji, a hint of urgency flashing in his eyes. "I can take you to a place—the deepest part of the Heavenly Realm, where the Seventh Chess Player fell ten thousand years ago. There you will find all the answers you need."

Chen Ji felt the Eye of Heavenly Mandate's aura approaching, that oppressive force causing everyone present's faces to turn pale. Han Lie's body trembled slightly, Ling Yuan even directly knelt on the ground—only Chen Ji and Shi Chen remained standing. Ye Qing gritted her teeth, struggling to maintain her footing, her Demonic Path mist being stripped away layer by layer by that pressure.

choice.prompt: The Eye of Heavenly Mandate's pressure approaches, and Shi Chen has made an invitation. Chen Ji must make a decision.

choices.description: The deepest part of the Heavenly Realm may hold the key to changing everything; there is no reason to refuse.

text.content: Chen Ji looked at the barrier about to collapse, then at Ye Qing, Han Lie and others, finally making his decision: "Very well. But I have one condition—they must leave safely." Shi Chen nodded: "Of course." He raised his hand, a golden light enveloping everyone, sending them out of the pressure range.

dialogue.content: Before Ye Qing was transported away, she desperately shouted at Chen Ji: "Chen Ji! You promised me you'd let me see the Holy Sect's downfall! You can't die!" Her voice carried unprecedented urgency. Chen Ji glanced back at her, the corners of his mouth slightly lifting: "Rest assured, I never break a promise."

choices.description: The Eye of Heavenly Mandate has arrived; leaving now is too dangerous. Better to temporarily avoid its edge.

text.content: Chen Ji shook his head: "Now is not the time. The Eye of Heavenly Mandate is here; if I leave with you, I would be exposing my back to all enemies." His tone was calm and firm. "If you have sincerity, first help me resolve the current predicament. Otherwise—forgive me, but I cannot entrust my life to someone I just met."

dialogue.content: Shi Chen gazed at him deeply, then smiled: "Good. You have courage." He turned toward the direction of the Eye of Heavenly Mandate's pressure, golden light blazing around him. "Since it's like this, I will block this crisis for you. But the next time—you must come." His figure transformed into a流光, charging toward the source of that pressure.

text.content: The Eye of Heavenly Mandate's pressure temporarily retreated under Shi Chen's resistance, but Chen Ji knew this was merely temporary calm. He lowered his head to look at the Tianji Record in his hand, the runes on the fragment flowing faster than ever before, as if responding to some summoning. Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded again, carrying a trace of fatigue: "Master, Shi Chen spoke the truth. The true purpose of the Tianji Record is to guide you on a path of God-Slaying. But the cost... indeed is足以让任何人陨落."

Chen Ji tucked the Tianji Record into his chest, his gaze casting toward the direction where Shi Chen had disappeared. The Chess Players of ten thousand years ago, the legacy of the Seventh Chess Player, the true ambition of the Eye of Heavenly Mandate... all clues pointed to one fact: this seemingly worthless fragment in his hand was born precisely to overturn Heavenly Mandate. And now, he finally knew what he must do—not become anyone's piece, but as a Chess Player himself, to overturn that chess game that had existed for ten thousand years.
